rationale: vol 2(AA).pdf p.15 / .doc L00333 (s.21 note (a)) and pdf p.111 / .doc L01826 (s.121 note 6). MML 2.pdf footnotes the s.21 reference as omitted by Act 37 of 1992 (p.12) and its s.121 note 6 (p.89) instead says the section prohibits a second trial by court-martial or a criminal court. The two editions therefore give opposite commentary on civil-court retrial after court-martial. Not resolved here; it is a legal question for the advisor and other agents.
advisor_questions: After omission of s.127 (6-9-1992), may a criminal court try a person already tried by court-martial for the same offence? Identify controlling authority.

claim: MML 1.doc Part I Ch II para 13 describes field punishment under AA s.75 as an available court-martial punishment; para 14 describes s.85 as permitting a CO to award a JCO only stoppages.
original_text: MML Part I Ch. II paras 13-14 (field punishment; summary punishments)
proposed_text: Proposal only: mark MML 1.doc Ch II para 13 as historical (pre-6-9-1992) and para 14's s.85 sentence as incomplete after Act 37 of 1992.
rationale: MML 1.doc L00041 (para 13) states that s.75 provides for field punishment and cites ARs 172-176; India Code [[page 27]] records s.75 omitted by Act 37 of 1992 w.e.f. 6-9-1992. Para 14 (L00043) on s.80/s.81 limits is consistent with India Code [[page 27]]-[[page 28]], but its account of s.85 (stoppages only) does not reflect s.85 as substituted by Act 37 of 1992, s.6, which adds severe reprimand or reprimand (not by an officer below Colonel) (India Code [[page 28]]-[[page 29]]; MML 2.pdf p.67 reproduces the substituted s.85). MML 1.doc is commentary of unknown date and predates the 1992 amendment on these points.
